_doc: Written only by node harness/bin/task.mjs. Phases run in order; P0 (ADOPT + STYLE DISCOVERY) waits for the owner by design and needs task.mjs signoff and task.mjs archsignoff before its gate passes. Later phases are added by the planner at the end of P0 (task.mjs phase-add) from the game's real state.

phases.name: Adopt, style discovery and architecture discovery
phases.goal: The harness drives the game (hook contract, verify, baseline perf), the old repo is audited, and the owner has signed off a style with budgets after side by side tests and an architecture after measured option benches.
exit: window.__game implements docs/GAME_HOOKS.md and the hooks_contract scenario passes
verify --quick and verify --all run green on the game as it is
baseline perf measured on this machine and written to harness/verify/perf_budgets.json
harness/design/STYLE_OPTIONS.md compares the candidate styles with test scene shots and measured frame times
the owner signed off one style (task.mjs signoff), STYLE_BIBLE.md and VERIFY.md look rules are written

harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md compares the architecture options with measured benches on this machine, including the map repair layer (harness/design/MAP_REPAIR.md: sources and licences, pipeline, rules, lane-level road model, map inspector, verification, pilot area), and the owner signed off an architecture (task.mjs archsignoff); TECH.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the chosen design
the phases after P0 are planned from the game's current state
the owner signed off a game design (task.mjs designsignoff); GAME.md has the fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan

tasks.title: Harness baseline on the scaffold: coordinate contract, drive scenarios, FD0
tasks.desc: The scaffold already has window.__game (src/debug/hooks.ts) and verify --quick was green on 2026-11-10. Lock the baseline and the coordinate rule (owner inbox: correct coordinates from day 1 with tests). (1) Check the hook contract against docs/GAME_HOOKS.md and fix any gap; without ?debug=1 window.__game.debug must not exist (add a unit test or a scenario that opens the page without debug=1). (2) Add src/geo/projection.ts: lat/lon to world metres and back around one named Delhi origin constant (India Gate, 28.612894 N, 77.229446 E), east +X, north -Z, up +Y, accurate to under 0.5 m within 25 km of the origin (local transverse Mercator or ENU; write the choice to decisions.md as provisional until the architecture sign-off). No mirroring, no axis flips. (3) Unit tests: the origin maps to (0,0); Connaught Place central park (28.6315, 77.2167) lands at x -1246 +/- 25, z -2071 +/- 25 (north-west of the origin); Red Fort (28.6562, 77.2410) lands at x +1129 +/- 25, z -4821 +/- 25 (north-north-east); round trip error under 0.01 m; a point due north has x 0 and negative z. (4) Scenarios (input only, wait in sim time): drive_north (throttle 3 s from heading 0: z falls by over 10 m, abs x under 0.5 m), drive_turn_right (throttle plus steer right: heading grows and x becomes positive), coords_north_marker (camera at the origin looking north shows the red north post in the centre third of the shot; the builder reads the shot). (5) Play script harness/verify/milestones/FD0.js per milestones.json FD0 (real inputs only). (6) quick.json: core = boot_title, hooks_contract, perf_baseline, drive_north; areas mapped to src/car.ts, src/geo/, src/debug/. Notes: this is tooling and tests, no look change.
accept: npm run typecheck and npm test pass; the projection tests named above exist and pass (CP and Red Fort within 25 m of the given x and z, round trip under 0.01 m)

node harness/bin/verify.mjs --only hooks_contract,boot_title,drive_north,drive_turn_right,coords_north_marker passes with no console errors, and the builder read coords_north_marker.png (red post centred, ahead)
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --milestone FD0 passes
a check proves window.__game.debug is undefined when the page opens without ?debug=1
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick passes and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --all passes (or each failure is listed as a known bug task)
decisions.md has the provisional projection entry; TECH.md 'Coordinates' names src/geo/projection.ts and its tests
tasks.summary: Transverse Mercator projection around India Gate, no flips; CP and Red Fort land within 25 m; drive_north, drive_turn_right, coords_north_marker, hooks_no_debug scenarios and FD0 pass; quick 7/7. verify --all deferred to the P0 gate (low usage mode).

tasks.title: Tooling: game design sign-off in task.mjs, gates, status and dashboard
tasks.desc: Owner direction 2026-11-10 (inbox mmwap8jxg): Phase 0 needs a third sign-off, the game design. Small tooling task, same pattern as signoff and archsignoff in harness/bin/task.mjs. (1) Add task.mjs designsignoff "<the owner's exact words>": writes designSignoff {at, quote} to harness/state/state.json and a decisions.md entry with the quote, journal line. (2) P0 gets designSignoff: true (through task.mjs, for example a small migration or a phase flag command; backlog.json is written only by task.mjs) and its exit list gains 'the owner signed off a game design (task.mjs designsignoff); GAME.md has the fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan'. (3) task.mjs gate P0 and gate --final fail without it, with a clear reason line. (4) task.mjs status prints 'game design sign-off: not yet ...' until recorded, like the other two. (5) The dashboard (harness/bin/dashboard.mjs) shows all three sign-offs (style, architecture, game design) with their state and quote. (6) Update the usage text, CLAUDE.md Phase 0 (one short paragraph 'd3. Game design discovery' and the gate line in step e) and add tests in harness/bin/ for the new command and gate reasons.
accept: npm test passes, including new tests: designsignoff writes state.json and a decisions.md entry; gate P0 lists 'No game design sign-off' until it is recorded
node harness/bin/task.mjs status prints the game design sign-off line; node harness/bin/task.mjs gate P0 output names the missing design sign-off
the dashboard page (node harness/bin/dashboard.mjs, http://localhost:4488) shows the three sign-off states (checked with a curl of the page or its JSON endpoint)
CLAUDE.md Phase 0 mentions the game design discovery and the third sign-off
tasks.summary: task.mjs designsignoff and phase-flag; P0 gate and gate --final require the design sign-off; status and dashboard show all three sign-offs; 10 new tests pass.

tasks.title: Salvage and quality audit of the old game (read only)
tasks.desc: Owner inbox part 1: a SALVAGE AUDIT of /Users/apple/Desktop/code/delhi-drive, read only (never edit, build, install, run npm or write there). Write harness/design/SALVAGE_AUDIT.md: one table row per item with verdict KEEP (copy after a check), REWRITE (keep the idea, new code), DROP, with evidence (file:line, numbers) and the reason. Cover: data sources and their licences (OSM PBF, Copernicus GLO-30 and why a surface model makes roads float or sink), bake knowledge in backend/worldBuilder/buildRegion.js (projection, tiling at zoom 16, 500 m tiles, binary format, what it did right and wrong), car tuning numbers and the handling model, the 580 frontend tests (read for intent: which checks are worth rewriting as tests here), assets in art-src and frontend/public (quality, licence, Delhi relevance: paan stains, political posters, textures), the lessons in README, TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md, docs/, TODO.md and CLAUDE.md, and the root cause of each base-layer failure: the mirror axis (worldGroup.scale.x = -1 and negated physics px), overlapping road meshes, misplaced railings, junctions that do not join, terrain and road misfit, tileManager.js at 2346 lines, the leftover cannon-es layer, the 11 GB JSON tiles. End with 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently' (one line each, feeds ARCH_OPTIONS). Then write harness/design/QUALITY_AUDIT.md from harness/design/templates/QUALITY_AUDIT.template.md, 'why it felt thin', scored against a polish and richness bar for a Delhi driving game (visuals, feel: handling, speed sense, camera, FOV, shake; audio: engine, horns, ambience; VFX: dust, smoke, skid marks, heat haze; traffic and life; UI and HUD; performance), every finding with evidence from the old game and a fix size, plus 'What to protect' (the good parts). Evidence for shots: if the already built frontend/dist can be served read only by a static server started from THIS repo (for example the harness static server pointed at that folder) without writing into the old repo, take a few shots and read them; if it needs its backend or fails, rely on code, docs and art files and say so. The owner reads both docs before the style interview, so put a 10 line summary at the top of each.
accept: harness/design/SALVAGE_AUDIT.md exists with a 10 line summary, the KEEP / REWRITE / DROP table (every row has file:line or a measured number as evidence) and the root cause section for each base-layer failure named in the desc
harness/design/QUALITY_AUDIT.md exists, follows the template headings, scores every area, and every finding has evidence and a fix size
git status shows no change under /Users/apple/Desktop/code/delhi-drive (cd there and run git status --short: empty or unchanged from before)
decisions.md has one entry per KEEP item that will be copied, with the reason (CLAUDE.md 'Copy from the old repo only after checking')
tasks.summary: SALVAGE_AUDIT.md (keep 3: handling and camera numbers, 4 CC0 sounds; base layer all dropped, root causes measured) and QUALITY_AUDIT.md (3 meet, 13 close, 14 far of 30). Old repo git status empty. Self-checked headings, decisions entries.

tasks.title: Game design options draft (GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY)
tasks.desc: Mode GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY (owner direction 2026-11-10, inbox mmwap8jxg: a car driving around Delhi is a tech demo, not a game). Write harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md with comparison tables and small text sketches (loop diagrams, a sample mission beat sheet, a HUD sketch) covering his 7 points: 1. fantasy options (new auto driver, delivery rider, cabbie who knows every gali, tourist guide, street racer, a mix), one sentence each plus why it fits Delhi; 2. the core loop at 30 s, 5 min and 1 h per fantasy, and the tension sources (traffic, time, money, rivals, police, weather, fares); 3. a big list (40 or more) of Delhi missions and activities (fares, deliveries, races, chases, festivals, wedding baraat routes, monsoon floods, rush hour, night runs, sightseeing tours past real landmarks, side jobs, collectibles) ranked by fun, uniqueness, build effort and map reuse; 4. progression and reasons to return (money, vehicle unlocks and upgrades, reputation by area, unlocking parts of the city, daily and weekly jobs, story or characters, personal bests and leaderboards, photo spots), each marked healthy or chore with the reason; 5. game feel (speed sense, near misses, horn culture, weaving through traffic, drifts, landmarks as rewards) and 3 candidate sets of feel pillars; 6. honest scope: the smallest first playable loop that is already fun in the pilot area (Connaught Place, ITO and Pragati Maidan, Chandni Chowk, one metro line), then what grows from it, each option with fun, cost, risk and needs from the map, AI traffic and art; 7. references (known open world and driving games): what fits, what to avoid; inspiration, never copy. Use the old game's modes (dash, taxi, delivery, free, police, see SALVAGE_AUDIT.md) as evidence of what was tried. End with a recommendation and at most 6 short, clear questions for round 1, each with options. Never invent the owner's answers.
accept: harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md exists with one section per point 1 to 7, a comparison table in each of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, at least 40 ranked missions and activities, and at least 2 sketches
a recommendation and at most 6 round 1 questions with options are at the end

tasks.title: Interview sitting 1: style, place and game design round 1
tasks.desc: The main session asks Anmol in short, clear rounds (AskUserQuestion if available, else plain questions) and waits. First show him the 10 line summaries of SALVAGE_AUDIT.md and QUALITY_AUDIT.md. Then follow harness/design/templates/STYLE_INTERVIEW.md rounds 1 (references and mood), 2 (concrete axes) and 2b (the place: Delhi landmarks, road types, signage and scripts, vehicles, street life, weather, light and time of day, materials). In the same sitting run game design round 1: show the GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md tables and sketches briefly and ask its round 1 questions (fantasy, core loop, first playable loop). Also ask the GAME.md 'As found' open questions (what the player does besides free drive, vehicles, day and night, traffic density, target hardware and browsers, size of the first playable area) and his first architecture preferences: is WebGPU-only acceptable or must WebGL2 work, how much disk the source data may use on this machine, is an offline bake on this machine fine. Record every answer verbatim with task.mjs inbox-add "<his words>" --source interview and ack it. Never invent an answer: a skipped question goes to the next round. Delhi world layers (harness/design/DELHI_WORLD.md, inbox mmwapw3co): show its 10 line summary, then ask (short, with options): (a) which landmarks matter most to you, which 2 or 3 are pilot heroes (proposal: Red Fort, Jama Masjid, CP inner circle or India Gate), and which others must be heroes later; (b) which areas to do first after the pilot (CP, ITO, Chandni Chowk are the pilot); (c) which metro line for the pilot (proposal: the elevated Blue Line stretch at Pragati Maidan and Indraprastha). Also ask the salvage audit's open questions (SALVAGE_AUDIT.md section 7): will the game be public or commercial (this decides FABDEM, believed CC BY-NC-SA, unverified); are invented parties and candidates fine on posters; is Euro Truck Simulator 2 still the quality reference; is a top speed near 110 km/h right for Delhi. Skipped questions go to P0-014.
accept: task.mjs inbox shows every answer recorded with source interview and acked
the answers are passed to the planner for the style options task (brief lists them)
the answers on hero landmarks, area order, pilot metro line, public or commercial, posters, ETS2 and top speed are recorded verbatim, or listed as skipped and carried to P0-014
the DELHI_WORLD.md answers are passed to the planner for P0-006 and noted for P0-018 (public or commercial decides the DEM licence check)

tasks.title: Style options draft, city brief and game design options update
tasks.desc: Mode STYLE_DISCOVERY with the round 1, 2 and 2b answers. Write harness/design/STYLE_OPTIONS.md from templates/STYLE_OPTIONS.template.md (reference board, 3 to 5 candidates, the comparison table with estimates, the fidelity levels for a city look: stylised low-poly city, stylised realistic, realistic PBR with baked lighting, photo-textured, each with honest performance cost at driving speed and asset volume for Delhi) and harness/design/CITY_BRIEF.md from templates/CITY_BRIEF.template.md (unconfirmed items marked). Name which 2 candidates go in style test batch A and which in batch B, and the ?style= name of each. Write the next round's questions (at most 6). Also update harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md with the game design round 1 answers (narrow the options, sharpen the recommendation, new sketches where they help) and write the game design round 2 questions (at most 6, short, with options). Delhi world layers (DELHI_WORLD.md): add a section 'Landmark tiers and area kits per candidate' to STYLE_OPTIONS.md: for each candidate, how a hero, a signature and a marker landmark look and two contrasting area kits (proposal: Chandni Chowk old city bazaar vs Lutyens bungalow road), the asset volume per tier (how many hero models, signature textures, kit atlases the city needs in that style and who makes them), and AI prompt fit for landmark models and kit textures. Put the landmark and area answers from P0-005 into CITY_BRIEF.md (Landmarks table with tiers) and update DELHI_WORLD.md section 9 (open questions) with what is answered.
accept: STYLE_OPTIONS.md and CITY_BRIEF.md exist and follow their templates; every number is marked estimate
each candidate has a ?style= name and is assigned to batch A or B
the questions for the next round are listed in STYLE_OPTIONS.md
GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md reflects every round 1 answer and lists the round 2 questions
STYLE_OPTIONS.md has the 'Landmark tiers and area kits per candidate' section covering every candidate, with asset volume per tier marked estimate
CITY_BRIEF.md Landmarks table lists the landmarks Anmol named with a proposed tier

tasks.title: Game design round 2 and later until the game design sign-off
tasks.desc: Show Anmol the updated GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md (tables, sketches, recommendation) and ask the round 2 questions, short and clear. May share a sitting with the style and architecture rounds. Record every answer verbatim (inbox-add --source interview, ack). Only his explicit words count as sign-off ('yes, go with the cabbie loop' counts; 'looks nice' or 'maybe' do not: ask him to confirm); record with task.mjs designsignoff "<his exact words>". If a round ends without sign-off: add a planner GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY update task and a new orchestrator task 'Game design round <n>', add each as a dep of the 'Game design record' task (task.mjs deps --add), then mark this task done with a note.
accept: every answer recorded and acked in the inbox
either task.mjs status shows the game design sign-off with his quote, or the follow-up round task exists and blocks the game design record task

tasks.title: Game design record: GAME.md, pillars and mission rules
tasks.desc: Only after task.mjs status shows the game design sign-off. Update harness/design/GAME.md with the signed fantasy, core loop (30 s, 5 min, 1 h), the 3 feel pillars (replacing the draft pillars), the mission and activity list with the first playable loop marked, the progression plan, scope guardrails, player verbs, HUD and the movement and camera feel numbers that the loop needs. Add the decisions.md entry with the sign-off quote. Make the standing rules concrete in harness/design/VERIFY.md 'Writing acceptance criteria': every mission task's acceptance includes fun criteria checked by a scenario, a play script or a named shot (clear goal shown within 5 s of start, a fair fail with a stated reason and an instant retry, a reason to retry such as a time or score to beat, a reward that matters shown on completion), and every phase plan lists how each of its tasks serves a pillar. Add milestones.json entries for the first playable loop's missions (required true) with summaries beat by beat.
accept: GAME.md has the fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan sections filled from the signed design; the draft pillars section is gone
decisions.md has the game design sign-off entry with Anmol's exact quote
VERIFY.md 'Writing acceptance criteria' has the fun criteria rule; milestones.json lists the first playable loop's missions

tasks.title: Delhi street stand-in scene and perf baseline
tasks.desc: The scaffold is a box on a plane, too empty to compare styles or measure anything real. Add a procedural stand-in Delhi street behind ?scene=street (default boot unchanged), built from CITY_BRIEF.md: about 300 m of a 6 lane arterial with a median and kerbs, a service lane, one signal junction, a stub flyover ramp (simple stand-in, not the lane model), footpaths, 40 to 80 box buildings with shopfront bands and sign boards, trees, street lights, a bus stop, 15 to 25 static vehicles (car, auto-rickshaw, bus stand-ins), a few people stand-ins, a debug.load id 'street' that puts the box car on it. Pure stand-ins, no assets needed; keep it in its own module (src/scenes/street.ts or similar) so style tests and benches reuse it. Then write harness/look_proof/poses.json with 6 views on it (car close-up, street at player height, junction, flyover ramp, HUD over play, busiest view from 40 m up; sim held, same moment every run), run node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --set baseline --perf, read the shots, and write draft budgets in harness/verify/perf_budgets.json (status stays draft) from the measured numbers with headroom, with the target filled in (machine, GL renderer, resolution, load). Delhi world layers (DELHI_WORLD.md): also add, in the same module or a sibling (src/scenes/landmarks_areas.ts or similar), procedural stand-ins for one landmark per tier (hero: an India Gate like arch from a small parts kit; signature: a domed tomb on a plinth or a CP style colonnade block; marker: an extruded footprint with an area material), each with its surroundings (lawn, wall, gate, parking), and two contrasting area kit blocks of about 100 m each (old city bazaar strip: tight shop houses, wires, signs, vendors; Lutyens bungalow road: walls, trees, low white bungalows), reachable by debug.load ids 'landmarks' and 'areas' (or placed along the street). Add 2 lookproof views to poses.json for them (tiers from the road at player height, the two area blocks side by side from 30 m up), so the poses become 8.
accept: node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --check passes and --set baseline --perf writes all 6 views and harness/look_proof/baseline/perf.json; the report quotes the machine, GL renderer and load
the builder read the 6 baseline shots: no blank or black frames, the street reads as a Delhi arterial (median, kerbs, shops, vehicles)
perf_budgets.json has draft numbers derived from the baseline with the target text filled in
a scenario street_boot (debug.load street, settle, shot) passes with no console errors; the default boot (no scene param) is unchanged: boot_title still passes
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick passes

scenarios landmarks_boot and areas_boot (debug.load, settle, shot) pass with no console errors; the builder read the shots: the three tiers are visibly different in detail and the two area blocks are visibly different
harness/look_proof/poses.json has the 2 extra views and the baseline set includes them

tasks.title: Architecture options draft (with map repair, lane model and map inspector)
tasks.desc: Mode ARCH_DISCOVERY. Write harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md from templates/ARCH_OPTIONS.template.md, using SALVAGE_AUDIT.md 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently', the baseline perf numbers, the style candidates and the owner's architecture answers from the interview, and the leading game design options (what the first playable loop needs from the map, traffic and physics). Decisions, 2 to 4 options each, every estimate marked: renderer (three.js WebGLRenderer vs WebGPURenderer with TSL and WebGL2 fallback, or another engine), physics (Rapier vs Jolt, main thread vs worker, vehicle controller), coordinates and projection (confirm or replace src/geo/projection.ts), world data pipeline and tile format (sizes, binary layout, compression), the map repair layer (refine harness/design/MAP_REPAIR.md: sources with licence and attribution and quality checks, pipeline, rule engine, auto-repair log, per-tile overrides, elevation solver, verification, pilot area), the lane-level road model (lane sets, Delhi class defaults, tapers, gores, flyover centre lanes climbing while service lanes stay at grade, never shared index points, continuity and overlap checks), the road graph to junction mesh builder (lane-edge curves, corner radii, kerbs, railings, no overlaps), terrain that conforms to roads (bare-earth DTM, flattening with shoulder blend), tile streaming and memory, instancing, LOD and impostors, textures (KTX2 and Basis vs WebP), the map inspector page (3D, linked from the dashboard, fly-to, proposed fixes as 3D preview lines with confidence and reasoning, writes per-tile overrides and the inbox, lane widths and splits shown; stack and port), and budgets per system. Confirm or rewrite the four bench tasks that follow this one (renderer, physics, pilot data and repair, lane road and terrain prototype) with task.mjs note or a desc change through REPLAN, so each measures what the table needs. Delhi world layers (harness/design/DELHI_WORLD.md): add decision rows for (a) the landmark registry pipeline: sources and matching (ASI list, Wikidata, Wikipedia and Commons as reference only, OSM tags, Anmol's named list), storage (landmarks.json plus overrides, schema), tier scoring, placement (footprint, orientation, plinth fit, landmark zone vs generated city), hero model limits (the 25,000 triangle and 3 material ingest limit vs a hero LOD chain or parts), stand-in parts kit; (b) the area profile pipeline: area division method (grid features, colony and ward seeds, which open sources), profile storage (archetypes plus per-area overrides), generator at bake time vs in the game, kits and atlases, edge blending, determinism; (c) the map inspector area and landmark views. Refine DELHI_WORLD.md with what changes and cross-link it from ARCH_OPTIONS.md. Make sure P0-016 measures an instanced area kit block (one atlas, many modules) and P0-018 covers the world layer sources.
accept: harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md exists, follows the template, has every decision named in the desc with 2 to 4 options, and marks every number as estimate or measured
harness/design/MAP_REPAIR.md is refined (sources with licence, rule list, overrides format, inspector) and cross-linked from ARCH_OPTIONS.md
each bench task in P0 names its ?arch= page or harness/bench/ script, its numbers and its harness/reports/arch/<name>.json output
ARCH_OPTIONS.md has decision rows for the landmark registry pipeline, the area profile pipeline and the inspector area view, 2 to 4 options each, every number marked
DELHI_WORLD.md is refined and cross-linked from ARCH_OPTIONS.md

tasks.title: Style tests batch A (2 candidates)
tasks.desc: Per harness/design/templates/STYLE_TEST_TASK.md, for the 2 candidates STYLE_OPTIONS.md assigns to batch A: render the street scene (and the default scene) in each candidate behind ?style=<name>, touching only render setup, materials, shaders, post passes, lights and a few procedural stand-ins, in one module per style (src/render/styles/<name>.ts). No gameplay, camera or UI logic change; without the param the look is unchanged. Time box: one build round and one fix round per candidate; a style that cannot be shown in that time is reported with what it would need. The style set includes the landmark tier and area kit views from P0-009, so each candidate shows how a hero, signature and marker landmark and the two contrasting area kits look in it.
accept: for each batch A style: node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --set style_<name> --query "style=<name>" --perf --no-build writes every view and perf.json judged against the draft budgets
node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --sheet baseline,style_<a>,style_<b> --out style_options writes harness/reports/look/style_options.jpg and the builder read it (downscaled to about 1600 px)
the default look is unchanged: lookproof.mjs --set baseline_check --no-build then --compare baseline_check --against baseline passes
verify --quick passes with no console errors
STYLE_OPTIONS.md has the measured numbers for both candidates in place of the estimates, wrong estimates marked
every style set has the landmark tiers view and the area kits view, and the sheet shows them for every candidate

tasks.title: Style tests batch B and the full side by side sheet
tasks.desc: Same as batch A for the remaining candidates (STYLE_OPTIONS.md batch B, 1 to 3 styles), then the full sheet of baseline plus every candidate. Same rules and time box as batch A. The style set includes the landmark tier and area kit views from P0-009, so each candidate shows how a hero, signature and marker landmark and the two contrasting area kits look in it.
accept: for each batch B style: lookproof.mjs --set style_<name> --query "style=<name>" --perf --no-build writes every view and perf.json
node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --sheet baseline,<every style set> --out style_options writes harness/reports/look/style_options.jpg with every candidate, and the builder read it
the default look is unchanged (baseline_check compare passes); verify --quick passes
STYLE_OPTIONS.md has measured numbers for every candidate and the sheet path
every style set has the landmark tiers view and the area kits view, and the sheet shows them for every candidate

tasks.title: Style comparison review
tasks.desc: Mode STYLE TEST for both batches: check every style set exists with all views and perf.json, read the sheet and at most 6 views, check the default look compare, check STYLE_OPTIONS.md numbers match the perf.json files. Report per candidate: shows the intended look or not, perf against the draft budgets, visible defects. This review stands in for per-task verification of the two style test tasks (low usage mode). Also judge per candidate: are the three landmark tiers distinct and readable, and do the two area kits read as different places.
accept: report lists every candidate with PASS or FAIL against its style test acceptance, with the perf numbers quoted from perf.json
any FAIL is a fix task added before the next style round

tasks.title: Style round 3 and later until the style sign-off (architecture round 1 in the same sitting)
tasks.desc: Show Anmol harness/reports/look/style_options.jpg and the STYLE_OPTIONS.md table with measured numbers, follow STYLE_INTERVIEW.md round 3 and later, record every answer verbatim (inbox-add --source interview, ack). In the same sitting show the ARCH_OPTIONS.md draft and ask its questions (benches are still to come). Only explicit words count as sign-off; record it with task.mjs signoff "<his exact words>". If a round ends without sign-off: add the refinement tasks it needs (planner STYLE_DISCOVERY update, builder style tweaks or a new candidate) plus a new orchestrator task 'Style round <n>', add each as a dep of the 'Style bible and budgets' task (task.mjs deps --add), then mark this task done with a note. Delhi world layers: show the pilot landmark census (harness/reports/arch/landmarks_pilot_draft.json, if P0-018 is done) and the 'Landmark tiers and area kits' section of STYLE_OPTIONS.md, and ask: confirm the pilot heroes, the hero list for later, the area order after the pilot, and any P0-005 question he skipped (public or commercial, posters, ETS2, top speed).
accept: every answer recorded and acked in the inbox

tasks.title: Style bible, look rules and signed budgets
